title: Set up a video editing team to make ads with an agent
summary: An agency lead rolled out a shared Claude Code ad-making skill to every editor; he says the team now makes Suno, Pixar and claymation-style ads under $100 per concept.
agent_role: Claude runs an animated-ad skill that generates the ads for each editor. Humans handle setup, training, budgets and cost tracking.
outcome: Author reports every editor can now make Suno, Pixar and claymation ads, at most $100 per concept and usually much less.
what_they_did: The poster put every editor on the Claude desktop app and pushed the ad-making skills to the whole organization at once. Each small team got its own spending key with a monthly budget. He ran setup calls until the animated-ad skill worked on each machine, then held one training and wrote one guide.
how_it_went: He says the team got to making Suno, Pixar and claymation ads this month. Each concept costs at most $100, and every ad's cost is logged in one sheet. Moving animated clips to a faster model cut generation from 2 to 6 minutes to about 45 seconds.
worth_knowing: He says the skill runs but nothing generates in the browser version, so use the desktop app. Keep the agent's permission setting on automatic, never on full bypass.
prompt: Help me run my ad-making skill for a new concept: [product or brand], style [animated / claymation / Pixar-like], length [seconds]. First write a short script and shot list and wait for my approval. Before generating any clips, estimate the cost and confirm it stays under [budget per concept]. After each generation, log the clip and its cost in [spreadsheet name]. Show me the draft cut before any final export.

curation.rationale: A real team rollout of Claude Code skills for making animated ads, with concrete setup rules, a cost cap and a speed figure. It lacks examples of the finished ads and step-by-step detail on the skill itself.
